haiku-low.q1: They see the generic message: "If an account exists for that address, we've sent a link." Nothing is created or sent.
haiku-low.q2: They get the generic message again. No token is created and no email is sent.
haiku-low.q3: A link works for 30 minutes after creation. It stops working sooner if it is burned, by use or by a newer link being issued.
haiku-low.q4: The link is not burned. It stays usable until it expires, so the user can retry.
haiku-low.q5: No sessions remain, including the current device, because all of the user's sessions are deleted. The user logs in again with the new password.
haiku-low.q6: The worker retries 3 times with backoff, then logs the failure and drops the job. The user is not told and sees no error.
haiku-low.q7: The raw token is generated and placed only inside the emailed link. Only its SHA-256 hash is stored.
haiku-low.q8: The server hashes the token from the link and finds the row with that hash. It checks whether the row is missing, expired after 30 minutes, or burned.
haiku-low.q9: It is counted from the user's reset_tokens rows created in the last hour, a rolling window. The document does not say how old rows are removed.
haiku-low.q10: Every earlier unused link for that account is burned, in the same transaction as inserting the new link's row.
haiku-low.q11: In one transaction: the password hash is saved, the token is burned, and all sessions are deleted. The confirmation email is queued after that.
haiku-low.q12: The token is checked again and burned in the same transaction as the password change, so two submits cannot both succeed. The locking mechanism is NOT STATED.

sonnet.q1: They see the generic message: "If an account exists for that address, we've sent a link." Nothing is sent.
sonnet.q2: The limit is 3 reset emails per account in a rolling hour, so the fourth request gets the generic message and no token or email is created.
sonnet.q3: 30 minutes from creation. It can end sooner if it is burned: used for a successful reset, or replaced by a newer link issued for the same account.
sonnet.q4: Still usable. The form shows an error, the token is not burned, and the link stays usable until it expires.
sonnet.q5: None. All of the user's sessions on every device, including the current one, are deleted. The user is redirected to the login page and logs in again with the new password (no automatic login).
sonnet.q6: The worker retries up to 3 times with backoff, then logs the failure and drops the job. The user is not told and nobody is notified. The user can request another link, which counts toward the hourly limit.
sonnet.q8: It hashes the token from the link and finds the row by that hash. The link is good unless the row is missing, expired (over 30 minutes) or burned (used time set). Otherwise it shows the expired-link page.
sonnet.q9: It is not kept separately. It is counted from reset_tokens rows created in the last hour. Old requests drop out because the window is rolling, so rows older than an hour are no longer counted.
sonnet.q10: All of the account's earlier unused tokens are burned (used time set). This happens in the same transaction as inserting the new row, so only one link works at a time.
sonnet.q11: In one transaction: save the new password hash, burn the token, and delete all of the user's sessions. The "your password was changed" email is queued after that transaction, followed by the redirect to login.
sonnet.q12: The token is checked again in step 3 inside the same transaction that changes the password and burns the token. Because the burn is in that transaction, two submits of the same link cannot both succeed. The document does not say what database mechanism (such as locking) enforces this.
